- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., price drops sharply after peak), model often fails to recognize it; add a 1–2 day lag correction in downward moves.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is mixed or neutral, model tends to overfit recent trends; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ price + sentiment-weighted adjustment.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often misses the shift; adjust forecast mid-horizon upward by 2–5% if sentiment >0.67 after day 10–15.
